description: 0.3.0 target architecture. Map 0 accepted by the owner; submaps and detailed contracts are provisional. Arrows are calls including their declared response, except explicitly named guidance/data/event arrows. No transitive access. Only 5 exposes shared part state; each other component may exclusively own private state. No source compliance has been established. Extension resource access added by owner request: Thingi10K belongs in Extensions, with an explicit external-resource wire. Extensions are unsandboxed local code; contracts describe intended SAAM/reviewed-extension structure, not confinement of arbitrary scripts. Owner confirmed preservation of a simplified Studio–agent channel, priority event batches and exclusive per-bundle editing; saved artifacts remain inspectable without regeneration dependencies. Specialized workspaces are external bundle producers with public engine access; handoff is one-way and does not grant confirmation authority.

nodes.label: Maker context
nodes.description: Guidance for the agent; numbered without pretending it is code.
notes: Inventory reviewed 2026-10-01 against actual guidance readers, CLI/MCP entry points and the skill catalog. Source references below are migration evidence, not scanned ownership or enforced contracts.

Group by how content is retrieved: one context reader, shared starting content, selected construction references, selected machine references, and Studio/tour participation. Source passages have one home even when several commands request them. A prose hyperlink is navigation, not a runtime component call.

Keep the map 0 boundary: context is delivered only to the agent. Installed extension manuals and discovery metadata belong in 4, accessed through the existing agent–Extensions interface; no hidden 1 → 4 loader. Geometry implementation remains the separate map 2 task.

The current reader can also expose builder/developer/history documentation. That allowlist is not the ownership of Maker context: BUILDERS.md, DEVELOPER-CONTEXT.md, CONTRIBUTING*.md, DECISIONS.md, DEVLOG.md, skill BUILDER/DEVELOPER manuals and implementation sections retain their own purposes. Maker-relevant sections in mixed files are identified below.

Current system can author these nodes, notes and contracts. It cannot bind Markdown sections or scanned declarations to them, track source freshness for these notes, enforce parent contracts, or certify conformance. Add inventory/source bindings and explicit unassigned/split-required/forbidden/unknown states before code assignment.

nodes.label: Read maker context
nodes.description: One reader selects startup, named references or task guidance; owns no part or Studio state.
notes: Current CLI access: maker-onboarding [--machine], read-guidance PATH#HEADING [--machine|--all], read-skill ID#HEADING, start-tour returned participation context, and inspect-generation-failure guidance. Direct startup reads AGENTS.md (CLAUDE.md points to it); onboarding does not repeat it.

Current MCP equivalents: maker_onboarding, read_guidance, read_skill and list_skills; runtime instructions, tool descriptions and onboarding reminders also deliver prose. These are evidence of existing delivery paths, not a decision to retain web/relay sessions in 0.3.0.

Candidate reusable code: core/agent/manuals.mjs::readManual, readGuidance, loadGuidance, assembleGuidance, guidanceSection, guidanceLinks, repositoryLinks, headings and gate parsing; core/agent/toolkit.mjs::contextPacket, readSkill and the context-only part of onboarding; core/agent/layers.mjs::onboardingSources, gatedIndex, machineHint and printHint; scripts/skill-digest.mjs::updatedSkillIndex.

Split mixed responsibilities instead of moving entire files: onboarding also fetches Git and probes dependencies; start-tour launches Studio; inspectFailure loads bundle state; runtime.mjs combines tool declarations, context and operational handlers. Only content selection/assembly belongs here.

Reuse one document/section selection mechanism for all four content groups, preserving IDs, anchors, links and omitted-section explanations. Direct file reads and tool wrappers select the same sources; do not add one reader implementation per group.

Machine-gated content needs explicit capability facts from the caller or owned published guidance metadata. Current manuals.mjs::machineOpens imports loadMachine: that dependency needs classification; do not smuggle an engine/private machine-state call through this bin.

Inventory schemas and command help as guidance too: scripts/agent-toolkit.mjs help, core/print/cli.mjs usage, adapters/mcp/src/runtime.mjs instructions/tool descriptions, and adapters/mcp/src/deposition-schemas.mjs. Operational schema validation stays with the API owner; prose/schema publication must be bound to the same contract, not copied into an independent schema.

notes: AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md: desktop entry routing, maker boundary, escalation pointers, tour-first rule and instruction to read local preferences. .local/AGENTS.md is checkout-owned guidance, not a release default or a globally published manual.
MAKERS.md: geometry/toolpath choice, interaction flow, assumptions and last-used settings, working boundaries, Studio reuse and command access. maker-onboarding returns this; start-tour reuses it.

core/print/USAGE.md: shared operation index, recipe edits and revision conflicts, nozzle selection, STL import/units/repair, spacing, generation/advisories/export, remembered setup and CLI forms. It is read in onboarding and by section; inspect-generation-failure reuses #check-generate-and-deliver, not a second failure manual.

skills/DIGEST.md and skills/catalog.mjs: existing discovery source contains 17 maker manuals (3 core families, 6 feature skills, 8 composition guides), plus builder-only mesh-tools outside maker context. Target starting context keeps core discovery and how to query Extensions; the 14 non-primitive manuals and their live discovery entries belong in 4.

Migration corrections, not implemented here: remove web-agent/relay workflow instructions, reflect Studio-triggered export, remove outdated delivery/approval ceremony, and route extension discovery through 4. Retain current content as evidence until its consumers migrate.

Export preparation, machine-axis/feed adaptation, startup/priming, material-change routines, encoding and exact-program interpretation belong in 8. core/print/workflow.mjs::createBundleWorkflow currently nests prepareGeneration, which calls generatePath then exportAndInterpretProgram: split that orchestration across the accepted boundaries.

Prefer one revision/lifecycle authority plus artifact storage and job/result handling, with narrow internal boundaries only where the inventory supports them; do not create three independently maintained notions of current/pending/valid.

Concrete migration seams: core/print/workflow.mjs mixes persistent commits, setup memory, generation, export/interpretation and approval/delivery. core/print/resolve-plan.mjs handles recipe resolution. Split only declarations that cross the accepted boundaries; retain proven persistence/validation algorithms.

The three Bundle → Studio contracts could share one revisioned snapshot/event interface. This is a proposal, not applied here; keep command authority and snapshot/event delivery explicit. Remembered setup needs a private owner and a declared source for the bundle snapshot.

Reusable seams include studio/viewer-renderer.mjs, material-view.mjs, toolpath-view.mjs, source-player.mjs, machine-session.mjs, agent-requests.mjs and studio-events.mjs. Server routes, subscriptions, tour and worker transport also need explicit homes; the three current boxes are provisional, not an exhaustive assignment.

Pre-export preview currently uses interpreted machine-program data. With Export only on the button, Studio must also present saved/generated SAAMpath before export. Inventory a SAAMpath-to-view conversion that reuses current renderers; do not generate a machine program secretly inside 3, 6 or 7 to preserve playback.
